text.p: Unseeded German Marc Goellner completed a week of triumphs over Spanish players on Sunday when he won the Marbella world series final by overpowering fourth-seeded Alex Corretja.
He clinched the match 7-6 7-6 after Corretja had saved five match points.
"It was my best-ever game on clay....I'd forgotten what it's like to win a tournament," said Goellner, whose only other major tournament win was in Nice in 1993.
In reaching the final Goellner had already knocked out Spaniards Tomas Carbonell, Francisco Clavet, Fernando Vicente and Felix Mantilla.
Corretja, who had not surrendered a set on his way to the final, struggled to match the German's powerful baseline game.
In front of a partisan Spanish crowd, Goellner, ranked 73rd in the world, dealt admirably with the pressure, particularly in the tie-breaks which he won 7-4 and 7-2.
